contentList.content: When you cast a spell that has the sole effect of restoring hit points, you lose no hit points from casting the spell, though it still counts against your total number of spell uses.
Serve as a prophet of hard truths, exposing deception and compelling honesty.
The number of martyr spells you can cast before a short or long rest. Casting a martyr spell also costs your own hit points.
You gain proficiency with Heavy Armour.
Ease suffering, heal the afflicted, and carry hope into the darkest places.
Once per long rest, when you would be downed, cling to life at 1 hit point instead.
Spread sacred havoc, upsetting the status quo through unpredictable violence and magic.
Redeem a stained past by shielding others and bearing punishment in their place.
Stand between the world and catastrophe, armed with prophetic magic against the coming end.
Break tyrants and free the oppressed through direct, often martial, rebellion.

Choose one creature you can see which can see you within 18m to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is Charmed or Frightened by you (the target's choice) for up to 1 minute. It can repeat this saving throw on each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. Once you use this ability, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
As a bonus action, gain temporary hit points equal to 1d10 + your level. Recharges on a short rest.
A divinely ordained warrior whose suffering is sacred. Martyrs spend their own hit points to fuel spells and turn pain into supernatural power.

You have learned to curry the gods' favor through anguish and mortal trials. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can lose 5 hit points to deal a bonus +10 necrotic or radiant damage (your choice) to the target. You don't make Constitution saving throws to maintain concentration on spells as a result of losing these hit points.

Starting at 11th level, you can lose 10 hit points to deal an additional +20 damage to the target.
Restore what war and civilization destroy, defending the balance of the natural world.

You can utter a prayer to the gods for mercy. As an action, you can spend Hit Dice and regain hit points as if you had just finished a short rest. When you use this ability, you can spend a number of Hit Dice up to your proficiency bonus.
Your death is appointed, but not yet due. When you fall to 0 hit points and begin to make death saving throws, you must fail 5 saving throws to die.
Speak with animals without paying the Martyr hit-point cost. Recharges on a short rest.

As a bonus action, either restore 1d4 + your Wisdom modifier hit points to another creature within 18m, or end the Blinded or Poisoned condition on a creature you touch. Once you use Balm, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
Your divine cause manifests itself upon you, forming a special mark or stigmata for all to see. You have Advantage on Persuasion checks.
If Torment kills its target, its self-damage is refunded.
Conquer, command, and demand submission in the name of cruel divinity.

You can reprimand those who draw your blood. When a creature you can see within 5 feet of you hits you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to deal that creature 1d6 necrotic or radiant damage (your choice). The damage increases by 1d6 when you reach 5th level (2d6), 11th level (3d6), and 17th level (4d6).
You regain all spent Hit Dice when you finish a long rest, instead of only half of them.

As a bonus action, for 10 turns nothing can hide from you: enemies within 3m of you lose invisibility, can't turn invisible or hide, and lose Blur, Mirror Image and Displacement. Once you use this, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
Hurl a spinning crescent of radiance: a ranged spell attack that deals 3d6 Radiant damage. If it misses, it arcs back and attacks the target once more.
Offer a sacrifice upon a pyre. Until your next long rest, you add your Wisdom modifier to your Armour Class instead of your Dexterity modifier. Can't be cast in combat.
Adds Wisdom modifier to Armour Class in place of Dexterity modifier.
Bind a creature's fate to your suffering. If it fails a Constitution saving throw, it takes 1d8 Radiant damage whenever you lose hit points, for as long as you concentrate.
Takes 1d8 Radiant damage whenever the martyr who cast this loses hit points.
Hold a moment of time in reserve. You have Advantage on your next attack roll within 10 turns.
Has Advantage on the next attack roll.
Raise a fleeting ward. The next 3 attacks made against you have a -10 penalty to hit.
The next 3 attacks against this creature have a -10 penalty to hit.
Touch a creature to ward it against dark magic until its next long rest: it has Resistance to Necrotic damage and can't be cursed or possessed.
Resistant to Necrotic damage. Can't be cursed or possessed.
A ring of holy fire erupts around you. Creatures you choose within 3m make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 4d6 Fire damage on a failure or half as much on a success.
A creature's bones harden like stone. Until the end of its next turn it has Resistance to non-magical Bludgeoning, Piercing and Slashing damage.
Resistant to non-magical Bludgeoning, Piercing and Slashing damage.
Creatures you choose within 3m of a point make a Constitution saving throw, taking 7d6 Necrotic damage on a failure or half as much on a success.
Touch a creature and it sprouts two extra arms for 10 turns, while you concentrate. It has Advantage on Athletics checks and can make a melee weapon attack as a bonus action.
Has two extra arms: Advantage on Athletics checks and a melee weapon attack as a bonus action.
Strike with your extra arms: a melee weapon attack.
Boomering arcs back if it misses: its attack roll has Advantage.
The next 2 attacks against this creature have a -10 penalty to hit.
The next attack against this creature has a -10 penalty to hit.

Identify the unique signature of a creature's blood and mark it as your quarry until your next long rest. It can't turn invisible, you don't have Disadvantage on attacks against it when it is heavily obscured, and once per turn when you deal damage to it you deal an extra [1]. A creature that is Bleeding automatically fails the saving throw.
Marked as a martyr's quarry. It can't turn invisible, its martyr doesn't have Disadvantage attacking it while it is heavily obscured, and deals extra Radiant damage to it once per turn.
Once per turn, deal extra Radiant damage to the creature you have Blood Printed.
Once on each of your turns, when you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, lose 5 hit points to deal an extra 10 Radiant damage to it. From 11th level, lose 10 hit points to deal an extra 20.
Once on each of your turns, when you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, lose 5 hit points to deal an extra 10 Necrotic damage to it. From 11th level, lose 10 hit points to deal an extra 20.
Burden spells are always prepared and don't count against the number of martyr spells you can prepare.
You have used Torment this turn.
Because your power is derived from mortal suffering, you can't regain hit points from any spell you cast.
Martyr Hit Dice, spent by Divine Healing. You regain half of them (all of them with Respite) on a long rest.
Spend Hit Dice to regain hit points.

Identify the unique signature of a creature's blood and mark it as your quarry until your next long rest. It can't turn invisible, you don't have Disadvantage on attacks against it when it is heavily obscured, and once per turn when you deal damage to it you deal an extra 1d4 Radiant damage for each level you cast it at. A creature that is Bleeding automatically fails the saving throw. Costs 5 hit points per level.

You can dive in the way of an attack. When a creature you can see attacks a target other than you that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to change the target of the attack to yourself instead.

Once you use this ability, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
An enemy is attacking an ally. Redirect the attack to yourself.
You cast a staff to the ground, which writhes and grows into a giant constrictor snake under your control. It fights alongside you until it is reduced to 0 hit points, for up to 1 hour.

Coil around a creature and crush it. On a hit it is grappled (escape DC 16) and Restrained until the grapple ends, and takes the crushing damage again at the start of each of its turns. The grapple ends if the snake moves away. The snake can't constrict another creature meanwhile.
Crushed in a giant snake's coils: grappled and Restrained, taking [1] at the start of each turn. Use an action to escape with a DC 16 Athletics or Acrobatics check.
Holding a creature in its coils. Can't constrict another creature until it lets go.
Try to break free of the snake's coils with a DC 16 check.
You can stoke the flames of chaos with your sword. When you hit a hostile creature with a melee weapon attack, you can roll on the table to the right to trigger an additional effect.
Skin turned to brittle glass: Armour Class reduced by 3.
Havoc! 6: Your foe bursts into flames
Havoc! 7: Your foe's skin turns to glass
Your magic carries the certainty of the end. When you roll damage for a spell, any die that comes up 1 is rolled again, and it can't come up 1 a second time.

A shimmering shield of energy surrounds a creature you touch. For the duration, ranged attacks with ballistic weapons (bows, crossbows, slings and firearms) and thrown objects have Disadvantage against it, and it has Resistance to their damage.
Ranged attacks with ballistic weapons and thrown objects have Disadvantage against this creature, and it has Resistance to their damage.
Restore 1d4 + your Wisdom modifier hit points to another creature within 18m. Uses Balm until you finish a short or long rest.
End the Blinded or Poisoned condition on a creature you touch. Uses Balm until you finish a short or long rest.
Within a Martyr's Maxim of Truth: can't be invisible or hidden, and loses Blur, Mirror Image and Displacement.
You use your Wisdom modifier instead of your Charisma modifier for Persuasion checks, if it is higher. Others can naturally sense when you are telling the truth.
